newsitem.title: INDIA: Ten injured in two blasts in Indian capital.
newsitem.headline: Ten injured in two blasts in Indian capital.

text.p: At least 10 people were injured on Tuesday in two small explosions in a crowded market district of New Delhi's old quarter, police said.
"Some ten or 11 people were injured," a police spokesman told Reuters by telephone, adding that most of the victims suffered leg injuries and none was in a serious condition.
"Both the blasts were of very mild intensity," Mahavir Singh, a Deputy Commissioner of police, said.

Police had earlier said there were three explosions, but the spokesman said there were two, one under a vegetable vendor's cart in Old Delhi's Subzi Mandi vegetable market, and another on a bus near a movie hall in the neighbourhood.
"It has been officially confirmed they were chemicals (which caused the explosions)," the police spokesman said. "The injured were hurt by acid or splinters from a metal container."
There was no immediate claims of responsibility for the blasts, but such incidents in the past in the Indian capital have been blamed on Sikh or Kashmiri separatists.

Crude bombs made of chemicals hidden in metal containers have been owned up by splinter Kashmiri guerrilla groups, among the dozens fighting Indian rule in the state of Jammu and Kashmir, mainly Hindu India's only Moslem majority province.
The first blast on Tuesday occurred around 6.55 p.m. (1325 GMT) in a city bus in front of a cinema hall in which two people were injured, Additional Commissioner of Police Satendra Nath said.
The second blast occurred at around 7.15 p.m. (1345 GMT) in front of the vegetable shop near the site of the first explosion.
Residents said the explosion in the vegetable shop could be heard up to a distance of one km (half a mile).
Shubh Prakash Sethi, owner of the vegetable shop, said: "I was selling vegetables when the blast occurred and I fell down from the place I was sitting."
"My friend who was sitting beside me fell unconscious." Sethi said.
